readings.title: The Covenant Framework
readings.subtitle: The Voice from the Heavens
readings.text: [Exodus 20:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke all these Words, saying, [2] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, out of the house of slavery.</dq> [3] <dq>“You have no other mighty ones against <dn>My</dn> face.</dq> [4] <dq>“You do not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of that which is in the heavens above, or which is in the earth beneath, or which is in the waters under the earth,</dq> [5] <dq>you do not bow down to them nor serve them. For <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> am a jealous <dn>Ěl</dn>, visiting the crookedness of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [6] <dq>but showing loving-commitment to thousands, to those who love <dn>Me</dn> and guard <dn>My</dn> commands.</dq> [7] <dq>“You do not bring <dn>את</dn> the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> to naught, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not leave the one unpunished who brings <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> Name to naught.</dq> [8] <dq>“Remember <dn>את</dn> the Sabbath day, to set it apart.</dq> [9] <dq>“Six days you labour, and shall do all your work,</dq> [10] <dq>but the seventh day is a Sabbath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. You do not do any work – you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your cattle, nor your stranger who is within your gates.</dq> [11] <dq>“For in six days <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> the earth, <dn>את</dn> the sea, and <dn>את</dn> all that is in them, and rested the seventh day. Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> the Sabbath day and set it apart.</dq> [12] <dq>“Respect <dn>את</dn> your father and <dn>את</dn> your mother, so that your days are prolonged upon the soil which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you.</dq> [13] <dq>“You do not murder.</dq> [14] <dq>“You do not commit adultery.</dq> [15] <dq>“You do not steal.</dq> [16] <dq>“You do not bear false witness against your neighbour.</dq> [17] <dq>“You do not covet your neighbour’s house, you do not covet your neighbour’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, or whatever belongs to your neighbour.”</dq> [18] And all the people saw <dn>את</dn> the thunders, <dn>את</dn> the lightning flashes, <dn>את</dn> the voice of the shophar, and <dn>את</dn> the mountain smoking. And the people saw it, and they trembled and stood at a distance, [19] and said to Mosheh, “You speak with us and we hear, but let not <dn>Elohim</dn> speak with us, lest we die.” [20] And Mosheh said to the people, “Do not fear, for <dn>Elohim</dn> has come to prove <dn>את</dn> you, and in order that <dn>His</dn> fear be before you, so that you do not sin.” [21] So the people stood at a distance, but Mosheh drew near the thick darkness where <dn>Elohim</dn> was.

readings.title: The Altar and the Servants
readings.subtitle: Restorative Justice and Freedom
readings.text: [Exodus 20:22] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Say this to the children of Yisra’ěl: ‘You yourselves have seen that <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you from the heavens.</dq> [23] <dq>‘You do not make besides <dn>Me</dn> mighty ones of silver, and you do not make mighty ones of gold for yourselves.</dq> [24] <dq>‘Make a slaughter-place of earth for <dn>Me</dn>, and you shall slaughter on it <dn>את</dn> your ascending offerings and <dn>את</dn> your peace offerings, <dn>את</dn> your sheep and <dn>את</dn> your cattle. In every place where <dn>I</dn> cause <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Name to be remembered <dn>I</dn> shall come to you and bless you.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And if you make <dn>Me</dn> a slaughter-place of stone, do not build <dn>את</dn> it of cut stone, for if you use your chisel on it, you have profaned it.</dq> [26] <dq>‘Nor do you go up by steps to <dn>My</dn> slaughter-place, lest your nakedness be exposed on it.’</dq> [Exodus 21:1] <dq>“These are the right-rulings which you are to set before them:</dq> [2] <dq>“When you buy a Hebrew servant, he serves six years, and in the seventh he goes out free, for naught.</dq> [3] <dq>“If he comes in by himself, he goes out by himself; if he comes in married, then his wife shall go out with him.</dq> [4] <dq>“If his master has given him a wife, and she has borne him sons or daughters, the wife and her children are her master’s, and he goes out by himself.</dq> [5] <dq>“And if the servant truly says, ‘I love <dn>את</dn> my master, <dn>את</dn> my wife, and <dn>את</dn> my children, let me not go out free,’</dq> [6] <dq>then his master shall bring him before <dn>Elohim</dn>, and shall bring him to the door, or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce <dn>את</dn> his ear with an awl. And he shall serve him forever.</dq> [7] <dq>“And when a man sells <dn>את</dn> his daughter to be a female servant, she does not go out as the male servants do.</dq> [8] <dq>“If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who has engaged her to himself, then he shall let her be ransomed. He shall have no authority to sell her to a foreign people, because of him deceiving her.</dq> [9] <dq>“And if he has engaged her to his son, he is to do to her as is the right of daughters.</dq> [10] <dq>“If he takes another wife, her food, her covering, and her marriage rights are not to be diminished.</dq> [11] <dq>“And if he does not do these three for her, then she shall go out for naught, without silver.</dq>

readings.title: Laws of Personal Injury
readings.subtitle: Life for Life
readings.text: [Exodus 21:12] <dq>“He who strikes a man so that he dies shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [13] <dq>“But if he did not lie in wait, but <dn>Elohim</dn> delivered him into his hand, then <dn>I</dn> shall appoint for you a place where he is to flee.</dq> [14] <dq>“But when a man acts presumptuously against his neighbour, to kill him by treachery, you are to take him even from <dn>My</dn> slaughter-place to die.</dq> [15] <dq>“And he who strikes his father or his mother shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [16] <dq>“And he who kidnaps a man and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [17] <dq>“And he who curses his father or his mother shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [18] <dq>“And when men strive together, and one strikes <dn>את</dn> the other with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but is confined to his bed,</dq> [19] <dq>if he rises again and walks about outside with his staff, then he who struck him shall be innocent. He only pays for lost time and sees to it that he is completely healed.</dq> [20] <dq>“And when a man strikes <dn>את</dn> his male or female servant with a rod, so that he dies under his hand, he shall certainly be punished.</dq> [21] <dq>“But if he remains alive a day or two, he is not punished; for he is his property.</dq> [22] <dq>“And when men strive and they shall smite a pregnant woman, and her children come out, yet there is no injury, he shall certainly be punished accordingly as the woman’s husband lays upon him. And he shall give through the judges.</dq> [23] <dq>“But if there is injury, then you shall give life for life,</dq> [24] <dq>eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,</dq> [25] <dq>burn for burn, wound for wound, lash for lash.</dq> [26] <dq>“And when a man strikes <dn>את</dn> the eye of his male or female servant, and destroys it, he is to let him go free for the sake of his eye.</dq> [27] <dq>“And if he knocks out <dn>את</dn> the tooth of his male or female servant, he is to let him go free for the sake of his tooth.</dq> [28] <dq>“And when an ox gores <dn>את</dn> a man or <dn>את</dn> a woman to death, then the ox shall certainly be stoned, and <dn>את</dn> its flesh is not eaten, and the owner of the ox is innocent.</dq> [29] <dq>“However, if the ox was previously in the habit of goring, and its owner has been warned, and he has not kept it confined, so that it has killed a man or a woman, the ox is stoned and its owner also is put to death.</dq> [30] <dq>“If a sin-covering is laid upon him, then he shall give the ransom of his life, whatever is laid on him.</dq> [31] <dq>“Whether it has gored a son or gored a daughter, according to this right-ruling it is done to him.</dq> [32] <dq>“If the ox gores a male or female servant, he is to give to their master thirty sheqels of silver, and the ox is stoned.</dq> [33] <dq>“And when a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls in it,</dq> [34] <dq>the owner of the pit is to repay, he is to give silver to their owner, and the dead beast is his.</dq> [35] <dq>“And when the ox of a man smites <dn>את</dn> the ox of his neighbour and it dies, then they shall sell <dn>את</dn> the live ox and divide <dn>את</dn> the silver from it, and also divide <dn>את</dn> the dead ox.</dq> [36] <dq>“Or if it was known that the ox was previously in the habit of goring, and its owner has not kept it confined, he shall certainly repay ox for ox, while the dead beast is his.</dq>

readings.title: Laws of Property and Restitution
readings.subtitle: The Premial System of Repayment
readings.text: [Exodus 22:1] <dq>“When a man steals an ox or a sheep, and shall slaughter it or sell it, he repays five cattle for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.</dq> [2] <dq>“If the thief is found breaking in, and he is struck so that he dies, there is no guilt for his bloodshed.</dq> [3] <dq>“If the sun has risen on him, there is guilt for his bloodshed, he shall certainly repay. If he has not the means, then he shall be sold for his theft.</dq> [4] <dq>“If the theft is indeed found alive in his hand, whether it is an ox or donkey or sheep, he repays double.</dq> [5] <dq>“When a man lets a field or vineyard be grazed bare, and lets loose <dn>את</dn> his livestock, and it feeds in another man’s field, he repays from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.</dq> [6] <dq>“When fire breaks out and spreads to thorn bushes, so that stacked grain, or standing grain, or the field is consumed, he who kindled <dn>את</dn> the fire shall certainly repay.</dq> [7] <dq>“When a man gives silver or goods to his neighbour to guard, and it is stolen out of the man’s house, if the thief is found, he repays double.</dq> [8] <dq>“If the thief is not found, then the master of the house shall be brought before <dn>Elohim</dn> to see whether he has put his hand into his neighbour’s goods.</dq> [9] <dq>“For every matter of transgression, for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for garment, or for whatever is lost which another claims to be his, let the matter of them both come before <dn>Elohim</dn>. And whomever <dn>Elohim</dn> declares wrong repays double to his neighbour.</dq> [10] <dq>“When a man gives to his neighbour a donkey, or ox, or sheep, or any beast to watch over, and it dies, or is injured, or is driven away while no one is looking,</dq> [11] <dq>let an oath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be between them both, that he has not put his hand into his neighbour’s goods. And the owner of it shall accept that, and he does not repay.</dq> [12] <dq>“But if it is indeed stolen from him, he repays to its owner.</dq> [13] <dq>“If it is torn to pieces, then let him bring it for evidence, he does not repay what was torn.</dq> [14] <dq>“And when a man borrows from his neighbour, and it is injured or dies while the owner of it is not present, he shall certainly repay.</dq> [15] <dq>“But if its owner was with it, he does not repay. If it was hired, he is entitled to the hire.</dq> [16] <dq>“And when a man entices a maiden who is not engaged, and lies with her, he shall certainly pay the bride-price for her to be his wife.</dq> [17] <dq>“If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he pays according to the bride-price of maidens.</dq> [18] <dq>“Do not allow a practiser of witchcraft to live.</dq> [19] <dq>“Anyone lying with a beast shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [20] <dq>“He who slaughters to an elohim, except to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> only, is put under the ban.</dq> [21] <dq>“Do not tread down a sojourner or oppress him, for you were sojourners in the land of Mitsrayim.</dq> [22] <dq>“Do not afflict any widow or fatherless child.</dq> [23] <dq>“If you do afflict them at all – if they cry out to <dn>Me</dn> at all, <dn>I</dn> shall certainly hear <dn>את</dn> their cry,</dq> [24] <dq>and <dn>My</dn> wrath shall burn and <dn>I</dn> shall kill <dn>את</dn> you with the sword, your wives shall be widows and your children fatherless.</dq> [25] <dq>“If you do lend silver to <dn>את</dn> any of <dn>My</dn> people, <dn>את</dn> the poor among you, you are not to be like one that lends on interest to him. Do not lay interest on him.</dq> [26] <dq>“If you take your neighbour’s garment as a pledge at all, you are to return it to him before the sun goes down.</dq> [27] <dq>“For that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What does he sleep in? And it shall be that when he cries to <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall hear, for <dn>I</dn> show favour.</dq> [28] <dq>“Do not revile an elohim, nor curse a ruler of your people.</dq> [29] <dq>“Do not delay giving your harvest and your vintage. Give <dn>Me</dn> the first-born of your sons.</dq> [30] <dq>“Likewise you are to do with your oxen, with your sheep. It is to be with its mother seven days. On the eighth day you give it to <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [31] <dq>“And you are set-apart men to <dn>Me</dn>, and you do not eat any meat which is torn to pieces in the field, you throw it to the dogs.</dq>
